data.title: What Hindustan Zinc Holders Saw Early
data.description:
If Hindustan Zinc sat on your watchlist instead of in your demat account, the last twelve months may feel like a missed call. For Hindustan Zinc shareholders, the return over the past year was 21.8%, including dividends. That result arrived in a year when bullish and bearish analysts were split on whether an India infrastructure and EV upcycle would outweigh circular economy headwinds. If you rewind to November 2025, how confident could you really be that infrastructure demand would matter more than rising recycling pressures?

The move put Hindustan Zinc in the middle of this trade. Scan 33 best rare earth metal stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Argument Hindustan Zinc Investors Faced Upfront

The shares cost ₹467 at the start of the period, and Hindustan Zinc holders had to decide which story about the future felt more reasonable.

The bullish narrative pinned a fair value of ₹564, a price level that flowed from assumptions rather than hard fact, built on the idea that revenue could grow 8.3% a year and margins could edge up from 31.3% to 32.0% by 2028.

The bearish view argued for a fair value of ₹335, tied to slower 4.7% annual revenue growth and concern that rising recycling and circular economy trends might cap demand for newly mined zinc.

What The Results Changed For Hindustan Zinc

The clearest marker was Hindustan Zinc’s Q2 2027 report. Revenue moved to ₹145,820 million and net income to ₹64,120 million, with net margin at 44.0% versus 32.0% a year earlier. That shift in profitability lined up more closely with the optimistic view that higher margins could matter more than recycling pressure, although long term demand risks stayed open.

The takeaway for you is simple. When an investment case leans on margin resilience, track net margin in the quarterly numbers and test whether it actually moves toward the story you were sold.

What Hindustan Zinc's Price Already Demands

Hindustan Zinc now trades at ₹568 after a 21.8% gain over the past year, while this Narrative’s Fair Value sits below the current price. The gap reflects concern that heavy expansion and diversification spend might not convert into equally strong long term returns.

For today’s level to hold up, you would need confidence that cost leadership and rising silver output can consistently fund growth projects and payouts without eroding cash generation.

"The numbers on volumes, margins, capital spending and payouts imply a share price that already bakes in successful execution on cost leadership, growth to roughly double metal capacity and higher value from silver and new minerals, with little room for disappointment."

Looking One Step Beyond Hindustan Zinc

Hindustan Zinc links you to metals used in construction and electrification. One step away, another miner focuses on a different metal entirely.

This company targets unhedged exposure to gold and copper, not zinc. That focus keeps its fortunes closely aligned with movements in the gold price.

Management is pursuing higher grade ore, longer mine lives and deeper underground expansions. The shared goal is more metal from every tonne moved.

It is also committing significant cash to new projects while buying back shares and paying dividends. The unresolved question is how that balance might shift if conditions change.

data.title: Can Elicio Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ELTX) Afford To Invest In Growth?
data.description:
Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. Having said that, unprofitable companies are risky because they could potentially burn through all their cash and become distressed.

Given this risk, we thought we'd take a look at whether Elicio Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ELTX) shareholders should be worried about its cash burn. In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

How Long Is Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Runway?

You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. When Elicio Therapeutics last reported its September 2026 balance sheet in November 2026, it had zero debt and cash worth US$31m. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through US$38m. Therefore, from September 2026 it had roughly 10 months of cash runway. That's quite a short cash runway, indicating the company must either reduce its annual cash burn or replenish its cash. You can see how its cash balance has changed over time in the image below.

See our latest analysis for Elicio Therapeutics

How Is Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Elicio Therapeutics isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. So while we can't look to sales to understand growth, we can look at how the cash burn is changing to understand how expenditure is trending over time. It's possible that the 3.2% reduction in cash burn over the last year is evidence of management tightening their belts as cash reserves deplete. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

How Easily Can Elicio Therapeutics Raise Cash?

Even though it has reduced its cash burn recently, shareholders should still consider how easy it would be for Elicio Therapeutics to raise more cash in the future. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By looking at a company's cash burn relative to its market capitalisation, we gain insight on how much shareholders would be diluted if the company needed to raise enough cash to cover another year's cash burn.

In the last year, Elicio Therapeutics burned through US$38m, which is just about equal to its US$37m market cap. Given just how high that expenditure is, relative to the company's market value, we think there's an elevated risk of funding distress, and we would be very nervous about holding the stock.

So, Should We Worry About Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Burn?

Even though its cash burn relative to its market cap makes us a little nervous, we are compelled to mention that we thought Elicio Therapeutics' cash burn reduction was relatively promising. After considering the data discussed in this article, we don't have a lot of confidence that its cash burn rate is prudent, as it seems like it might need more cash soon.
